payload.text: Note Why would I use a static factory method when a constructor performs the work of creating an object already? In Chapter 13, I’ll describe a pattern called Identity Map. An Identity Map component generates and manages a new object only if an object with the same distinguishing characteristics is not already under management. If the target object already exists, it is returned. A factory method like create() would make a good client for a component of this sort.

payload.markdown: For the User class, not much clever needs to happen. The DomainObject constructor calls getGroup() and finds it locally. In the case of SpreadSheet, though, the search begins at the invoked class, SpreadSheet itself. It provides no implementation, so the getGroup() method in the Document class is invoked. Before PHP 5.3 and late static binding, I would have been stuck with the self keyword here, which would only look for getGroup() in the DomainObject class.

items: Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constructor: __construct initialises each new object; promoted parameters collapse the boilerplate.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Identity Map: One object per row per request, so repeated reads return the same instance.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Static & Constants: Members belonging to the class itself rather than to any one instance.

8241.title: Late Static Bindings: The static Keyword
8241.code:
<?php
abstract class DomainObject
{
    private string $group;

    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->group = static::getGroup();
    }

    public static function create(): DomainObject
    {
        return new static();
    }

    public static function getGroup(): string
    {
        return "default";
    }
}

// listing 04.58
class User extends DomainObject
{
}

// listing 04.59
class Document extends DomainObject
{
    public static function getGroup(): string
    {
        return "document";
    }
}
// listing 04.60
class SpreadSheet extends Document
{
}

// listing 04.61
print_r(User::create());
print_r(SpreadSheet::create());
